title: Run-length encoding with strict decoding
requirements: encode writes each run as its count followed by the character ('aaab' -> '3a1b'), and decode(encode(s)) == s for any digit-free string
encode raises ValueError if the input contains digits
decode raises ValueError on malformed input (missing count, trailing count, zero count)
(after the user switch) long runs use multi-digit counts instead of 9-chunks ('a'*12 -> '12a')
user_messages: rle.encode / rle.decode: each run is the count then the char, so 'aaab' → '3a1b'. decode has to give back exactly the original

digits in the input can't be encoded unambiguously, so encode raises ValueError on them. decode raises on junk (missing count, count with nothing after it, zero count). split runs longer than 9 into chunks of 9
actually don't split at 9 — just write the real count, 'a'*12 → '12a'. simpler to read
